newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies close with pared losses.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies close with pared losses.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures pared losses late with shortcovering cited in hogs and evening up in pork bellies ahead of the USDA Cold Storage report, traders said.
Hog futures closed mostly 0.025 to 0.375 cent lower, with April off 0.100 at 78.950 cents a lb. Pork bellies ended down 0.350 to 1.200, with March off least at 74.500 cents.

Shortcovering and renewed demand by locals with cash connections erased most of the midsession losses in hog futures. Early sellers turned buyers when selling interest waned near midsession lows, traders said.

However, resistance was still evident from from continued weak cash markets. Expectations had been for cash hogs and pork products to turn up but demand never developed for either and this prompted the early selloff, they said.
Cash hogs are called steady to weak again early next week as expectations are now for slack demand to continue for cash pork products, they added.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $1.38 at $70.79 per cwt.

Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien bought late after selling early along with Rosenthal Collins. In hog options, commercials bought June 82 calls and sold June 74 puts late. Volatility was unchanged, pit sources said.

Pork bellies also rebounded somewhat on scattered profit taking and evening up ahead of the Cold Storage report. A weak product market and concern about product going into storage weighed on the market early, traders said.
The mixed short covering offset selling by R.J. O'Brien, Refco and LIT division of First Options late, pit sources said.

Analyst expectations on the report ranged from 39.7 to 43.2 million lbs in frozen storage on February 1 compared with 46.5 million last year. Stocks rose during January compared with a 10-year average decline of 130,000 lbs, they said.
